events.text: At four you are taught to sit on a cushion for an hour without moving while ministers bow to you. The rule is that you may not scratch your nose. Your nose has never itched so much in its life.

effects.log: You do not scratch. The Grand Chancellor nods at you as if you had passed an examination. You think perhaps you have.
The whole hall pretends not to see. One old minister hides a smile in his sleeve, and from then on he is your favourite.

events.text: Every morning a food taster eats a spoonful of your rice before you do. One morning the taster, a quiet boy only a few years older than you, stops chewing and goes pale. It is only a fish bone. The whole kitchen is dismissed anyway.

effects.log: The taster stays. Years later he still bows to you a little lower than the rules require.

choices.text: Learn the names of the cooks

effects.log: You learn all nineteen. The palace is not a building, you begin to understand. It is people.

events.text: The Emperor takes you up onto the walls of the Forbidden City at sunset and points at the roofs of the capital, thousands of them, smoking with evening fires. "All of that," the Emperor says, "will be heavy." You do not understand. You remember it anyway.

effects.log: The Emperor laughs, and does not answer, and carries you back down on one shoulder.
You get to two hundred before the sun goes down. You decide to come back tomorrow for the rest.

events.text: A painted kite from the southern gardens lands in your courtyard with a note tied to its tail: Prince Seoryun's mother sends it, the Noble Consort Gwi. It is a beautiful kite. Your nurse burns it in the brazier without a word.

effects.log: Your nurse holds you until you stop. "Beautiful things from that palace," she says, "have needles in them."
Your nurse tells you, in a whisper, how the last Crown Heir died. You sleep with the lamp on for a month.

events.text: Nobody watches a younger royal very closely. You discover a gap behind the Hall of Literary Glory where a drain runs under the wall, and on the other side of it, the whole capital: noodle stalls, puppet shows, a man who swallows fire.

effects.log: You learn the capital the way other royals learn the classics. A noodle seller calls you "the little official" and gives you extra.

choices.text: Tell nobody, and never go back

effects.log: You keep the gap a secret the way other children keep a frog in a box. One day it might matter.

events.text: At a palace banquet the Crown Heir is seated beside the Emperor and you are seated beside a pillar. Nobody speaks to you for three hours, so you watch: who toasts whom, who does not drink, who looks at the doors.

effects.log: By the end of the night you know which three ministers hate each other. You are seven.

choices.text: Slip under the table and go to sleep

effects.log: A servant carries you home asleep. The Emperor, someone tells you later, asked where you were.

events.text: The old gardener of the Imperial Garden lets you help prune the plum trees. He does not seem to know or care who you are. "Cut where it wants to be cut," he says. "Not where you want."

effects.log: You learn every tree in the garden by name. The gardener says you have patient hands, the first praise anyone has given you.
He was a sword master once, it turns out, before his knees. He shows you a stance with a pruning knife. You practise it in secret.

events.text: Princess Ahyeon, a half-sister a year older than you, finds you crying behind the Hall of Mental Cultivation and does not ask why. She sits down beside you, takes out two candied hawthorns, and gives you the bigger one.

effects.log: The beginning of the longest friendship of your life costs one candied hawthorn.

choices.text: Give it back and take the smaller

effects.log: "You are strange," Ahyeon says, and laughs, and from then on finds you every day.

events.text: The Cold Palace is not cold, exactly. It is quiet. The paint is peeling, the servants are old, and your mother sings to you in a dialect from the south that no one else in the Forbidden City speaks.

effects.log: You learn eleven of them. When you sing one in the main palace by mistake, a eunuch looks at you very hard.
Your mother tells you the truth, gently: she said the wrong thing to the wrong woman. You decide to say the right things, always.

events.text: A box of sweet rice cakes arrives at the Cold Palace with no card. Your mother looks at it for a long time, then feeds one to the stray cat that lives under the steps. The cat sleeps for two days and wakes up very confused.

choices.text: Bury the rest in the garden

effects.log: You bury the cakes under the oldest tree. Nothing grows there for a year.
You keep it in a lacquered box under your bed. One day someone will ask what it is.

events.text: The Emperor walks past the gate of the Cold Palace on the way to the Spring Rite and stops for one breath, then walks on. You are standing in the gateway in your best robe. You do not know whether you were seen.

effects.log: A guard stops you, kindly. "Next year," she says. Her name is Mok Jinhwa, and she remembers your face.
Your mother sees you bow to nothing, and has to go inside for a while.

events.text: The other royal children are forbidden to play with you. One of them, Princess Ahyeon, climbs over the wall of the Cold Palace every third day anyway, tears her robe on the tiles, and lies about it.

effects.log: Ahyeon sings them badly and loudly all over the palace. Nobody can prove where she learned them.

choices.text: Tell her to stop, to keep her safe

effects.log: "No," says Ahyeon, and comes the next day with a ladder.

events.text: You are a hostage at a foreign court, which means you are fed well, dressed well and watched always. Your keepers call you "our guest". The children of the court call you something else, until you learn their language well enough to answer back.

effects.log: You answer back in their own tongue, and better. The children stop. One of them laughs and offers you a horse.
You learn it quietly, perfectly, and never let on how much you understand. It is a useful thing to be underestimated.

events.text: A letter comes from home, the first in two years. It is from the Emperor and it is three lines long: the harvest was good, the borders are quiet, and you are to be obedient. You read it eleven times.

effects.log: You write nine pages. You will never know if anyone read them, but writing them helps.

choices.text: Fold it into a paper boat

effects.log: You float it down the palace canal. Your keepers report it. Somewhere at home, someone frowns.

events.text: The foreign ruler's youngest child, a solemn little royal called Ilan, decides that you are their best friend. Ilan's nurse disapproves, Ilan's tutors disapprove, and Ilan does not care in the least.

effects.log: You spend a whole summer catching frogs in the moat with the heir of the people who keep you prisoner. It is the best summer you have.
Ilan is hurt, but keeps trying. Someone on this side of the border likes you, at least.

events.text: War talk at the foreign court: the border garrisons are restless. Your keepers move you to a smaller room without a window. A hostage is a promise, and promises are the first things broken.

effects.log: You read every book they will give you. When the talk dies down they move you back, slightly embarrassed.
By the end of the month the guards bring you dumplings and news. One of them says he would not have done it, if the order came.

events.text: In the coldest hour of a winter night something vast and golden moves across the moon above the Forbidden City. The guards on the walls fall to their knees. It turns its great head, once, and looks down at your window.

effects.log: You look back. It blinks, slowly, the way a cat does at someone it has decided to allow. The Yellow Dragon of the dynasty knows your face now.
You hide. In the morning there is one golden scale on your windowsill, warm as bread.

events.text: Grand Tutor Baek Ilsu is eighty years old, has taught three emperors, and falls asleep during your recitations. When you stop reciting, he opens one eye and tells you the line you skipped.

choices.text: Recite the whole Book of Rites

effects.log: It takes until dark. Baek Ilsu does not fall asleep once. "Adequate," he says, which from him is a great deal.

choices.text: Ask him what the emperors were really like

effects.log: "Frightened," says Baek Ilsu, "every one of them. The good ones knew it." He gives you a list of books that are not on the list.

events.text: Baek Ilsu sets you a question for the palace examination, the one the scholars sit: "When the people and the throne want different things, which is the throne?" You have a week.

effects.log: Baek Ilsu reads your essay twice and burns it. "Correct," he says, "and never write it where anyone else can read it."
He nods, and marks it, and says nothing. You are not sure you passed.

choices.text: Answer that the question is wrong

effects.log: He laughs until he coughs. "You will be either a great ruler or a dead one," he says, "and I would like to see which."

events.text: Behind a sliding bookcase in Baek Ilsu's study are manuals the palace pretends do not exist: the internal arts. "An emperor who cannot feel poison in a cup," the old tutor says, "does not need to know much else."

effects.log: You learn to breathe the way the murim breathes. For the first time your body feels like something you own.
Baek Ilsu shuts the bookcase. "Wise," he says, sounding disappointed. "Mostly."

events.text: Captain Mok Jinhwa of the imperial guard is the only person in the palace who will hit you. In the training yard she knocks you down nine times before breakfast and helps you up nine times, without a word.

effects.log: You get up a tenth time and she lets you land one blow. "There," she says. "Now you are a little dangerous."
"Because someone will try to kill you," Mok says, "and I would like you to make it difficult."

events.text: At the autumn hunt your horse bolts into the pines. When you get it under control there is an arrow in the tree beside your head that was not meant for a deer. Captain Mok is there a moment later, very calm and very white.

choices.text: Pull out the arrow and keep it

effects.log: The fletching is dyed the green of the southern palace. Mok sees it too, and says nothing, and doubles your guard.

choices.text: Laugh it off for the court

effects.log: You ride back laughing. The court is impressed. Someone in it is very disappointed.

choices.text: Ask Mok to swear to you

effects.log: Mok looks at you for a long moment. "Not yet," she says. "Ask me when you are older. I may say yes."

events.text: Captain Mok finds you at dawn in the training yard, practising alone. She watches for a while. Then she kneels, which a captain of the guard does only for the Emperor, and offers you the hilt of her sword.

effects.log: "My sword to you," she says, "and not to the throne, if the two are ever different." It is treason. You will keep it secret your whole life.

choices.text: Refuse it, to keep her safe

effects.log: "That is why I offered," Mok says, and stands, and it is never mentioned again. She guards your door anyway.

events.text: Prince Seoryun is your age, clever, handsome, and the son of Noble Consort Gwi. At the Lantern Festival he finds you alone on a bridge and says, pleasantly, that one of you is going to be emperor and the other is going to be dead.

choices.text: Say it does not have to be like that

effects.log: Seoryun looks at you as if you are speaking a foreign language. Then, for a second, as if he wishes you were right.
You smile. Seoryun smiles back. Two royal children on a bridge, smiling, while the lanterns float by.
You walk away. Behind you, Seoryun laughs, not unkindly. It is the worst sound you have ever heard.

events.text: Princess Ahyeon is to be sent to a foreign khan's court, to buy ten years of peace. She tells you on the palace roof, swinging her feet over the edge, as if it were nothing.

choices.text: Go to the Emperor for her

effects.log: You kneel in the Hall of Mental Cultivation for a whole afternoon. The journey is put off two years. Ahyeon does not speak to you for a week, then hugs you so hard it hurts.
You teach her everything the foreign court taught you, or everything the books did. "If I must go," she says, "I will go armed."
You do not say anything. Neither does Ahyeon. It is the right thing to say.

events.text: You overhear Noble Consort Gwi in the Imperial Garden, speaking softly to Chief Eunuch Gong Bo about "the accident" that will happen at the Dragon Boat Festival. Neither of them knows you are behind the rockery.

effects.log: You tell the Emperor everything. Whether the Emperor believes a child over a Noble Consort is another matter.

choices.text: Simply stay away from the river

effects.log: You fall ill on the morning of the festival, very convincingly. Nobody drowns. Gwi sends you a get-well gift.
The Chief Eunuch goes very still. Then he bows. From now on the Inner Court is a little more yours than hers.

events.text: Noble Consort Gwi invites you to tea, alone. She is charming, beautiful and very kind, and she asks a great many questions about your health, your tutors, and which door of your palace you use at night.

effects.log: Nothing happens. That, you realise on the way home, was the message: she could have.

choices.text: Pour it into the plant pot when she looks away

effects.log: The plant is dead by morning. You have learned something, and so, from the pot, has she.

choices.text: Answer every question with a lie

effects.log: You give her a wrong door, a wrong tutor and a wrong illness. Gwi is very pleased. You are very pleased.

events.text: Prince Seoryun falls from his horse at the spring hunt and lies in the mud with a broken leg, far from the others. You are the only one who sees. Nobody would ever know if you rode on.

choices.text: Ride for help, and stay with him

effects.log: You splint his leg with your own sash. Seoryun says nothing the whole time. At the end he says, "I will not forget this." You are not sure how he means it.
You ride on. Someone else finds him at dusk. He never knows. You always will.

events.text: Ilan, the foreign heir, has grown solemn and tall and is learning to rule. Over a game of go in the summer palace Ilan asks you, quietly, what your empire's generals say about theirs.

effects.log: You tell the truth. Ilan thanks you and never asks again. You have given away something, and you are not sure what.
Ilan smiles. "Good," Ilan says. "I would think less of you if you had answered."
Ilan laughs and tells you. Two hostages of fortune, trading secrets over a go board.

events.text: The foreign court's master of arms takes an interest in you: a hostage who does not cry and does not complain. He teaches you their horse archery, which your own empire's generals would give a great deal to learn.

effects.log: You learn to shoot from the saddle at a gallop. Someone at home will be very interested in that.

choices.text: Learn it, and keep it to yourself

effects.log: You learn it and decide it belongs to you, not to any general.

events.text: You are sixteen. Under the treaty the hostage may go home now, or stay. The foreign ruler summons you and says, with what looks like real regret, that there would be a place for you here. Ilan stands behind the throne, not looking at you.

effects.log: You thank the foreign ruler and ask for your horse.
You kneel to the court that raised you.

choices.text: Ask for a year to decide

effects.log: The foreign ruler grants it. At eighteen the treaty will decide for you.

events.text: At the capping ceremony the Emperor places the cap of a grown royal on your head with hands that shake a little. The whole court bows. As you straighten, you see Prince Seoryun across the hall, bowing lowest of all, and smiling.

choices.text: Bow back to Seoryun, just as low

effects.log: The court murmurs. Seoryun's smile slips, for a moment, into something like respect.
The Emperor sees it, and nods, very slightly. The heir to the cap is watching only the throne.
Mok is by the door, in full armour, watching the crowd and not you. That is how you know she is on your side.

events.text: Your capping is small: a side hall, a minor minister, half the incense the Crown Heir had. Grand Tutor Baek Ilsu comes anyway, on two sticks, and sits in the front row, and is the only one who claps.

effects.log: You kneel to your tutor before the court. It is not the rite. Baek Ilsu cries, and pretends it is the incense.
The minister is surprised to be thanked. Ministers remember being surprised.

events.text: Baek Ilsu has you read the memorials the Emperor receives, the real ones, with the flood reports and the bribes. "Now tell me," he says, "which minister is lying."

effects.log: "Always the honest-looking one," Baek Ilsu agrees. "Good."

choices.text: Say they all are, a little

effects.log: "Correct," says the old man. "Now find the one lying the most."

events.text: The foreign court's scholars let you sit in on their debates. They argue about your own empire's history as if it were theirs, and get it confidently wrong.

effects.log: They are annoyed, then interested. One of them writes your corrections down.
You learn more about your homeland from its enemies than from any book at home.

events.text: Captain Mok makes you fight three of the guard at once in the rain. You lose, badly, and the guards help you up and call you "Highness" in a different voice afterwards.

effects.log: You lose tomorrow too, but less. Mok almost smiles.
The guards eat to your health. A guard who has shared your dumplings is a guard who hesitates before an order.

events.text: You spend the year being pleasant to people: the scholars of the Pure Stream, the eunuchs of the Inner Court, the generals, the Dowager's clan. It is harder than any sword drill.

effects.log: The Generals like a royal who rides. You ride a great deal.
The Pure Stream like a royal who reads. You read in public, ostentatiously.
Everyone thinks you secretly favour them. It is exhausting, and it works.

events.text: At a banquet the Grand Chancellor Bang Mujin takes your arm and walks you along the lake. He talks about the weather, the harvest and the Emperor's health, in that order, and only the last one matters.

choices.text: Ask about the Emperor's health directly

effects.log: Bang Mujin smiles. "Your Highness is direct," he says. "Directness is expensive at court."
You talk about the weather for an hour. Bang Mujin leaves thinking you are either very clever or very stupid. Either suits you.

events.text: Princess Ahyeon and you sit on the palace roof, as you did as children, and plan the succession like a game of go: who will support whom, who must be won, who must be watched.

effects.log: "If you are emperor," Ahyeon says, "nobody sends me to a khan." You promise. You mean it.
Ahyeon looks at you sideways. "You sound like the Emperor," she says. It is not entirely a compliment.

events.text: Prince Seoryun receives you in his own palace, which is larger than yours, and serves you the same tea his mother served you once. He watches you look at it. Then he drinks from your cup first.

effects.log: You drink. Something changes between you. Not friendship, yet. A truce.
Seoryun sighs. "Then we will both be sorry," he says.

events.text: The Cold Palace again. The paint peels further every year. Your mother pours your tea with the same care as when you were six, and asks after your health before her own.

effects.log: She takes your face in her cold hands. "Live first," she says. "Then promise."
You sing one of her songs, badly. She laughs until she cries. The guards outside the gate pretend not to listen.

events.text: The Cold Palace's gate stands open for the first time in your life, and nobody is guarding it. The Emperor's pardon came this morning. The lady who raised you on southern songs stands in the gateway in her old court robe, which no longer fits, looking at the sky.

effects.log: You walk out together into the main palace. The court lines the path, bowing. Noble Consort Gwi is not there.
She walks out alone, slowly, and then turns and holds out her hand to you after all.

events.text: Chief Eunuch Gong Bo, who knows everything that happens inside the palace walls, offers you a gift: the name of the minister who has been reporting your movements to Noble Consort Gwi. The price is a favour, later, unnamed.

effects.log: You learn the name. You also learn what it is to owe the Inner Court.
Gong Bo bows. "Your Highness will find out anyway," he says. "Only later, and less cheaply."

events.text: The Emperor is coughing at audience now. The court watches the coughs the way farmers watch a sky. Ministers who never visited your palace begin to visit it.

effects.log: You receive them all, smile at them all and trust none of them. Your allies grow; so does the list of people watching you.
You sit by the bed and read the Emperor the reports aloud. The Emperor falls asleep holding your sleeve.

events.text: A flood in the south. The Emperor, testing you, gives you the relief: the silver, the granaries, and the governors who have been stealing from both for ten years.

effects.log: The south eats. The governors keep their heads, and owe you them.

choices.text: Make an example of the worst governor

effects.log: One governor is stripped and sent to the frontier. Every other governor in the empire sends you a gift.

choices.text: Go yourself, in a plain robe

effects.log: You carry sacks on the dykes for a week. Nobody believes it until the stories reach the capital.

events.text: The Grand Chancellor Bang Mujin proposes, gently, that if the Emperor should die, a young ruler would benefit from a wise regent. He does not say who he has in mind. He does not need to.

effects.log: Bang Mujin is pleased. You have made a friend, and possibly a master.

choices.text: Say the empire needs no regent

effects.log: Bang Mujin smiles and says of course. His people stop visiting your palace.

choices.text: Ask him what the regent would want

effects.log: "Only to serve," says Bang Mujin. You both laugh, politely, for slightly too long.

events.text: Princess Ahyeon writes from the khan's court, where she was sent after all. The letter is cheerful, full of horses and snow, and in the margin, in tiny characters, are the names of three of your enemies' agents.

effects.log: Three of Gwi's people are quietly dismissed. Ahyeon, from a thousand miles away, is still guarding you.
You write about horses and snow, and in the margin, in tiny characters, that you miss her.

events.text: Prince Seoryun comes to you at night, alone, without his mother's people. "She will not stop," he says. "I am not sure I want her to win. I am not sure I want you to."

choices.text: Offer him a place, whoever wins

effects.log: Seoryun looks at you for a long time. "I will think about it," he says, which from him is a great deal.
"I am choosing," Seoryun says. "That is why I came." He leaves before dawn.

events.text: The ministers have made a match for you, for an alliance: a royal of a foreign court, whose portrait arrives on a silk scroll. The portrait is very flattering. The treaty attached to it is very long.

effects.log: You sign the treaty.
You return the portrait with great courtesy.
The ministers are scandalised. The match waits on the decision.

events.text: The match is with the child of one of the great houses of the court, whose family has six generals and a grudge against Noble Consort Gwi. Your betrothed meets you in the Imperial Garden and says, frankly, that neither of you chose this.

effects.log: You shake hands like two merchants closing a deal. It is a better start than most.
"Thank you," says your would-be betrothed, with real relief.
You talk until the lanterns are lit. It is the first honest conversation either of you has had at court.

events.text: Your betrothed turns out to be Ilan, the solemn child of the foreign court where you grew up. The treaty is a peace treaty. Ilan writes one line in the margin: "I did not ask for this. I did not refuse it either."

effects.log: You write one line back: "Neither did I."
You refuse, and write to Ilan yourself, at length, so that Ilan knows it is not about Ilan.

events.text: A note under your teacup, in Chief Eunuch Gong Bo's careful hand: a list has been drawn up, and your name is on it. It gives no date. Gong Bo does not give dates for free.

effects.log: You burn it. Your hands are steady. You are rather proud of that.
You count, on your fingers, in the dark. The answer is not enough fingers.

events.text: Captain Mok comes to your palace in plain clothes, which she never does. She does not sit. "The guard on your gate has been changed," she says. "Not by me."

effects.log: "Leave," says Mok, "or let me stand there myself. Not both."

choices.text: Thank her and send her away, for her safety

effects.log: Mok goes. She is back at your door within the hour, in armour, and does not ask permission.

events.text: From the Cold Palace a maid brings you a single southern song, sung under her breath as she pours the water: the one about the bird that leaves the nest before the snake arrives.

effects.log: You understand it. The Cold Palace has heard something, behind the walls where nobody thinks to stop listening.
The maid smiles and goes. The next verse is the one where the bird comes back.

events.text: The morning after: the broken lanterns on the steps have been swept away before sunrise, and the court pretends nothing happened. The guard on your gate is Captain Mok's again. You are alive, and the palace knows exactly why.

choices.text: Thank the guard, one by one

effects.log: You learn the names of every guard who stood at your gate. You never forget them.

choices.text: Go to audience as if nothing happened

effects.log: You walk into audience on time, smiling. The court decides you are not a royal who is easily frightened.

events.text: Captain Mok Jinhwa is buried with the honours of a general, at your order. Nobody at court asks why a captain of the guard deserves a general's tomb. They know.

choices.text: Carve the oath on her stone

effects.log: You have one line carved: My sword to you. Only a few people alive understand it.
You stand at the grave until dark. Whatever comes next, it will not be for nothing.

events.text: With Noble Consort Gwi sent away to a convent and Prince Seoryun to a frontier post, the palace is very quiet. Ministers bow lower. Servants walk faster. You have won, and the palace is afraid of you.

effects.log: You write that his post is honourable and his life is safe. He writes back one word: understood.
You enjoy it a little. Then you catch yourself enjoying it, and do not like what you see.

events.text: The Emperor is dead. The bells of the Forbidden City ring for a whole day and night. In the Hall of Supreme Harmony the throne stands empty under its golden canopy, and the whole court is looking at the royal children.

choices.text: Kneel by the coffin all night

effects.log: You keep the vigil until dawn. The court notes who knelt longest.
Your allies meet you in the dark: generals, scholars, a eunuch or two. Nobody says the word throne. Everybody means it.

events.text: The Grand Chancellor Bang Mujin comes to you before the bells have stopped, carrying the imperial seal in a yellow silk box. He does not open it. "Your Highness is young," he says. "The empire is old. Let me help."

effects.log: Bang Mujin explains the regency in great detail. It is a very comfortable cage.

choices.text: Ask him to open the box

effects.log: He hesitates for exactly one breath too long. Now you know what he wants.

events.text: Prince Seoryun stands at the other end of the hall in his mourning white. Noble Consort Gwi is beside him, very still. Seoryun looks at you across the coffin and, very slightly, shakes his head: not like this.

effects.log: You nod. Whatever happens next, the two of you will not be the ones who start it.
You look away. When you look back, Gwi is watching you instead.

events.text: The coronation takes a whole day. The nine steps. The nine kowtows of the court. The Yellow Dragon of the dynasty, carved into the ceiling above the throne, seems to watch you sit down. Somewhere a bell rings that has not rung since the last reign began.

effects.log: For a moment you are sure it looks back.
Hundreds of backs, bowed. Every one of them a person you now answer for. The Emperor was right: it is heavy.

events.text: The Yellow Dragon comes to the coronation. It coils around the roof of the Hall of Supreme Harmony in broad daylight while the whole capital watches, and when you come out it lowers its great head until its whiskers touch the steps.

effects.log: You bow to the dragon. The capital will tell the story for a hundred years.

choices.text: Lay a hand on its head

effects.log: Its scales are warm as summer stone. It knew you as a child. It knows you now.

events.text: The Grand Chancellor Bang Mujin sets the crown on your head with perfect ceremony, and then takes the seat beside the throne, one step lower, where the regent sits. When the court bows, it bows to both of you. It rises looking at him.

effects.log: You smile. You endure. You begin, very quietly, to count your friends.
Bang Mujin meets yours, and inclines his head, and you both understand the game has only begun.

events.text: Exile is a small house in a far province, a magistrate who visits once a month to see that you are still there, and a garden. The first night you cannot sleep for the silence. The second night you sleep for twelve hours.

effects.log: You plant plums, like the old gardener taught. Something of the palace grows here after all.
You write to every ally you had. Some write back. A few write back carefully, in code.

events.text: You stay at the court that raised you. Your homeland strikes your name from the yellow register. Ilan comes to your rooms that evening with a pot of plum tea and two cups, and does not say anything at all, which is exactly right.

effects.log: A royal of two courts, and now of one. It is enough.
You look east until the stars come out. Then you close the shutters and go to bed in the only home you have known.

events.text: Outside the walls of the capital you sell your jade belt to a pawnbroker for a fraction of its worth, buy a plain robe and a road sword, and walk south. Nobody looks at you twice. It is the most wonderful feeling in the world.

effects.log: You walk until your feet blister. The palace grows small behind you, then disappears.
You look back once at the golden roofs. Then you do not look back again.

events.text: The Grand Chancellor signs your edicts for you, in your name, with your seal, which he keeps. At audience you sit on the Dragon Throne and say the words he has written. Afterwards a young official waits behind a pillar to bow to you, and only you.

effects.log: His name is Cha Unbyeol. He has three friends. They have friends. It is a beginning.
You walk past. A puppet who makes friends is a puppet who is watched.

events.text: A memorial reaches your desk that the Grand Chancellor has not read: a governor's report of famine, which Bang Mujin buried. Someone put it here on purpose.

effects.log: You send grain through a back channel. The famine eases. Bang Mujin never learns who did it.
Bang Mujin thanks you warmly and the governor is dismissed. You are not sure who won.

events.text: On the anniversary of your coronation you go up onto the walls of the Forbidden City at sunset, alone, and look at the roofs of the capital smoking with evening fires. Heavy, the old Emperor said. You understand now.

effects.log: You count to two hundred and stop, smiling. Some things you can finish in one life.

choices.text: Go down and walk among them

effects.log: You walk the night market in a plain robe. A noodle seller gives you extra and does not know why.

events.text: Princess Ahyeon comes home from the khan's court as an envoy, grey at the temples, and kneels to you in the throne room. You come down the nine steps and lift her up before she can finish, in front of the whole court.

choices.text: Give her a seat at your side

effects.log: Ahyeon sits at your right hand at the banquet. Nobody at court ever again mistakes who your friends are.

choices.text: Take her up onto the palace roof

effects.log: You sit on the roof with your feet over the edge, two old royals, and eat candied hawthorns.

events.text: Prince Seoryun, grey and weathered from the frontier, asks for an audience. He kneels and asks for nothing at all, only to see the capital once more before he dies.

choices.text: Give him a palace in the capital

effects.log: Seoryun lives out his years in the capital, writing a history of the frontier. It is very good.

choices.text: Let him see it, and go back

effects.log: He sees it, and goes back. At the gate he bows to you, deeply, as an emperor.

events.text: A rider in the colours of the capital comes to your house in exile with a sealed letter. Your hands shake opening it. It is from an old ally at court: the throne is weak, and some of the court remember you.

effects.log: You burn it. You have a garden, and a life, and you do not want them to end in the capital.
You write back. Nothing will happen for years. But you are no longer only an exile.

events.text: In the sect's practice yard an elder watches you hold your sword and frowns. "Where did you learn to stand like that?" the elder asks. "That is a palace guard's stance." Every disciple in the yard turns to look.

choices.text: Say you learned it from a guard

effects.log: It is the truth, and not the whole truth. The elder lets it go, for now.
You change your stance on the spot. It is harder to hide where you came from than you thought.

events.text: On a mountain road you meet a palace eunuch travelling in plain clothes, who stops, stares, and then bows to the ground in the dust. "Highness," he whispers. "They said you died of a fever."

effects.log: He gets up slowly, looks at you once more, and says, "Yes. I am mistaken." He tells no one.

choices.text: Ask him for news of the palace

effects.log: He tells you everything. When he leaves you sit on a rock for a long time, a royal again for one afternoon.

events.text: Passing the walls of the Forbidden City you stop dead. You know, without knowing how, exactly where the drain runs under the wall behind the Hall of Literary Glory, and what the noodle stall beyond it smelled like.

effects.log: The drain is there. The noodle stall is gone. Your soul has been here before.
You walk on. Some doors are better left shut, even in a past life.

events.text: In a temple far from the capital there is an old painting of an emperor on the Dragon Throne. The face is worn away by centuries of incense. You stand in front of it far longer than you mean to, and the monk lights a stick for you.

effects.log: You bow. It feels like bowing to yourself, which is strange, and also not.
"An emperor who was born to it," the monk says. "They say the dragon loved that one."

events.text: A cup of tea is set in front of you by a stranger, and your hand stops a finger's breadth from it. You do not know why. Your heart is hammering. Somewhere in a past life, a cup like this one ended everything.

effects.log: You pour it away. It was only tea. Your soul does not believe that, and never will.
It is only tea. You drink it, and something in you that was very old lets go.

events.text: In a far province you pass a small house with a garden of very old plum trees, planted in rows the way a palace gardener plants them. You know, somehow, which tree was planted first.

effects.log: The bark is rough and warm. You were an exile here, once, and happy.
"Some royal, long ago," says a neighbour. "Very good with plums."

events.text: At a play in the market square an actor in a paper crown recites the lines of a puppet emperor: the edicts someone else wrote. You find you know every word before the actor says it.

effects.log: You do not want to see how it ends. You know how it ends.

choices.text: Stay, and clap loudest at the end

effects.log: In the play the puppet takes back the seal. You clap until your hands sting.
